reasons.E: The medieval gown's tall wimpled hennin makes the most distinctive outline of the five from the ARPG camera, a spire no other look in the game has, over a deep plum bell with a fur band; it reads as noble at once.
reasons.C: The rococo gown is the most elegant: faded rose and dove grey under black bows, a tiered bell skirt whose fall shows in the side view, and a small tilted cap; its colour stands apart from every family.
reasons.A: The Victorian mourning gown, a veiled broad-brimmed hat over a high-necked black bodice, bustle and tiered skirt, is the most gothic and sits best in the night-bound world.

fixes.E: The hennin is very tall for a helm: check in Studio that it clears doorways and the camera, and that the trailing sleeve drapes don't cut into a swinging arm.
fixes.C: The skirt's thigh and shin panels show seams from the front; widen the shin panels so the two tiers meet into one bell standing still.
fixes.A: All black and slate, it can merge into the night from the high camera: lift the bone lace trims a step so its outline holds on dark ground.

notes: 5 of 6 survived (the cathedral gown never finished). Gowns are heavy work: 4 of 6 ran out of 70 turns and 1 overran Claude Code's 32K reply cap on the first pass; resuming them cost cents, not a rerun, and gowns now get 100 turns and DeepSeek 64K replies. Every gown is 90 to 100 parts, so all of them need PerfBudget.armour.parts raised to about 100 (from 64) in the game, or trimming by a third, before they can merge. Two gowns' puffed shoulders (B, D) read as pauldrons from above; a note on sleeve scale would help the pack.
